verdict_reason: Both fixes are correct and I re-derived and re-measured each. (a) The alpha inversion: Steele's MST theorem gives E_alpha(n) ~ n^((d-alpha)/d), so the log-log slope is m = 1 - alpha/d and d = alpha/(1-m) -- the code's new form -- not 1/(1-m). Measured on uniform clouds of known dimension, the estimate is now flat in alpha where it previously scaled as 1/alpha: true d=2 gives 2.010/1.944/1.917/1.914/1.918/1.922/1.909 at alpha = 0.25/0.5/0.75/1.0/1.25/1.5/2.0, true d=5 gives 5.006/4.650/4.543/4.486/4.454/4.430/4.421, true d=8 gives 8.155/.../6.727. (b) Parity at the shipped alpha = 1.0 is preserved BIT-EXACTLY: against the official ArGintum/GPTID PHD.fit_transform with the global legacy RNG seed-matched, absolute difference 0.000e+00 on three clouds (1.926514658062, 4.509278358478, 8.781406596445). (c) max_length: 512 is now pinned in defaults.yaml and matches cache.py:405, which truncates at 512, so the cached and uncached paths build the same cloud.
comparable_reason: PHD is dimensionless with no structural d_model or n_layers term and the standing 66-model sweep backs that up (rho +0.196 d_model p=0.11, +0.210 n_layers p=0.090, -0.084 vocab_size, +0.133 n_params -- none significant). What limits comparability is the POOLED cloud, which I re-measured this round on 81 WikiText documents per model: distilgpt2 pooled 8.9757 against a per-text mean of 6.4749 +/- 1.1090 (+38.6%), gpt2 pooled 6.3188 against 5.0383 +/- 0.9537 (+25.4%). Pooling mixes per-document manifolds and the inflation is not a constant -- it is 1.386x for one model and 1.254x for the other on the SAME corpus, so it does not cancel in a cross-model comparison. num_samples also counts DOCUMENTS, so tokenizers that segment more finely contribute more rows before the 2000-point cap, and no uncertainty is emitted alongside the point estimate even though the per-text spread is 15-18% of the value.
github_reason: Imported the official IntrinsicDim.py and ran PHD.fit_transform against _phd_dimension on identical clouds with the global legacy np.random seeded to match BLME's RandomState draw order (n_reruns=1): absolute difference 0.000e+00 on all three cases. Read the reference source directly to confirm the alpha claim: fit_transform ends `m = np.mean(ms); return 1 / (1 - m)` with no alpha term at all, while prim_tree does raise edge lengths to self.alpha -- so the official code IS wrong for alpha != 1, and BLME now deliberately differs there. That is the right call, but the task can no longer claim to reproduce GPTID exactly across the alpha range, only at alpha = 1.0.
paper_reason: Tulchinskii et al. 2023 Table 1 publishes PHD = 9.491 +/- 1.010 for Wikipedia articles with RoBERTa-base embeddings. The campaign's paper-protocol run (per-text clouds, adaptive grid) gave 9.233 +/- 1.120, relative error 2.72%, with official GPTID on the identical clouds at 9.238 +/- 1.187 -- BLME is as close to the published number as the authors' own code. What I re-verified this round is that the estimator producing it is bit-exact to GPTID and that the alpha change does not disturb it (alpha = 1.0 is unchanged). The SHIPPED pooled values do not sit in that band: 6.32 for gpt2 and 8.98 for distilgpt2 here, and 4.7-21.6 across the zoo.
confounds_reason: Standing 66-model measurement: no architectural parameter reaches significance (max |rho| = 0.210 at p = 0.090). Nothing in this round's diff affects that -- the alpha correction is a no-op at the shipped alpha = 1.0 and the max_length pin only makes the cached and uncached paths agree. Worth restating that 'not a size proxy' is not 'well behaved': values are sharply non-monotone within a family (gpt2 6.31 -> gpt2-medium 4.73 -> gpt2-large 16.54), far beyond the estimator's own seed noise of sd 0.0625.
defects: ANSWERING THE JUDGEMENT QUESTION: implement the per-text protocol; renaming is the weaker option. The per-text run is cheap -- 81 documents per model took under a minute each on one GPU in this round's measurement -- it reproduces the published 9.491 to 2.7% where pooling does not, and it yields a standard deviation (1.109 on distilgpt2, 0.954 on gpt2) that the pooled point estimate discards. Since the per-model inflation factor is not constant (1.386x vs 1.254x on the same corpus), renaming to pooled_corpus_phd would preserve a quantity whose bias varies by model, which is worse for a cross-model study than fixing the protocol. Recommendation: emit phd_dimension (per-text mean) and phd_dimension_sd as the headline, keep the pooled value as phd_dimension_pooled for continuity, and only then is dropping the paper anchor unnecessary.

Stale docstrings after the alpha fix. _phd_dimension's Returns section still says 'Estimated intrinsic dimension d = 1 / (1 - m)' and the PHDimensionTask class docstring still says 'E(n) ~ n^{(d-1)/d} (alpha=1), d = 1/(1-slope)'. Both now describe the OLD formula. The module also claims to reproduce GPTID exactly, which is true only at alpha = 1.0 now that the reference's alpha bug is deliberately not reproduced.

No uncertainty is emitted. Only seed = 42 is reported. Estimator-seed noise alone is sd 0.0625 on distilgpt2 (0.7% of the value); with the max_points cap draw resampled the earlier rounds measured 3.5%-7.5%, and the cap draw IS part of the shipped pipeline.

Parity coverage stops at n_reruns = 1, because that is the only setting where the reference's threaded global-RNG stream can be matched. The shipped config is n_reruns = 3, so the configuration actually run in the study has no bit-parity test, only an equal-in-distribution argument.

alpha remains config-reachable in defaults.yaml. The fix makes any value of alpha give roughly the same answer (2.010 down to 1.909 on a true-d=2 cloud across alpha 0.25-2.0), which is the correct behaviour, but the residual drift is systematic and downward with alpha and with d (true d=8: 8.155 at alpha=0.25 falling to 6.727 at alpha=2.0), consistent with the theorem's requirement alpha < d. Worth a docstring note that alpha should be kept well below the expected dimension.

MINIMAL_CLOUD = 80 is enforced as a hard error floor where the reference leaves it an unreferenced module constant. Harmless, arguably better, but a deviation from the 'reproduces GPTID EXACTLY' claim.

Measured this round, that changes distilgpt2 from 8.976 to 6.475 +/- 1.109 and gpt2 from 6.319 to 5.038 +/- 0.954, and it is the version that reproduces the paper's 9.491 to 2.7%. Update the two stale docstrings that still say d = 1/(1-m) and the 'reproduces GPTID EXACTLY' claim (now true only at alpha = 1.0, because the reference's alpha handling is a bug BLME deliberately does not reproduce). Add a distributional parity case at n_reruns = 3 so the shipped configuration has coverage. Emit _meta_phd_seed_sd over 3-5 full seeds with the cap draw included.
